summary: Masahiro Takano (b. 1960) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also served as a librarian as attested in 1995.

Masakatsu Fujita (b. 1949) specializes in philosophy and Japanology. Educated at Kyoto University (~1968–1977), he headed its History of Japanese Philosophy department (~2000–2014) and served as representative of the Kyoto Philosophical Society (attested 2006).

Masakazu Tanaka (b. 1955) works in religious studies. He studied at Tohoku University and earned a Ph.D. from the London School of Economics/University of London. He was an assistant professor at Kyoto University (1988–2019) and became vice president/professor at PIIF in 2019.

Masako Keta (b. 1953) is a philosophy and religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University, notably under Yoshinori Takeuchi. She held posts at Hamamatsu University School of Medicine, Nanzan, Kanazawa University, and served as Kyoto University's professor of philosophy of religion (2000–2018).

Masamichi Asukai (1934–2000) was a Japanology and history scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1953–1963) and later held an academic post there from ~1968 to 1998, where he taught Peter Francis Kornicki.

Masamichi Ichigo (b. 1941) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Otani University, Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao, Susumu Yamaguchi, and Yuichi Kajiyama, as well as in the US. He held professorships at Kyoto Sangyo University and Otani University.
Masamichi Sakai is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna, where he was supervised by Helmut Krasser in 2006.
Masanori Nakagawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer (attested 1991) and associate professor in the Faculty of Literature (attested 2002) at Chikushi Jogakuen University.

Masanori Shono works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He has held positions as an assistant professor at Osaka University (attested 2012) and as a researcher at the University of Munich (attested 2015).

Masao Abe (1915–2006) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University, UTS, and Columbia. He held professorships at Kyoto Women's University, Otani, Kyoto University, Hanazono, and Nara University of Education (1952–1980), later teaching at University of Hawaiʻi.
Masao Shizutani (b. 1923) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and history. He held assistant professor posts at Josai University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (attested 1974).
Masaru Akimoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as a professor in the Faculty of Contemporary Society at Kyoto Women's University (attested 2002, 2015).

Masashi Nagai (b. 1946) is a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Komazawa University (doctorate 1998). He spent his career at Komazawa University as lecturer, associate professor, professor emeritus (2017), and president (2019), and directed the Museum of Zen Culture and History.

Masataka Suzuki (b. 1949) specializes in religious studies, history, and Japanology. After studying at Keio University (~1968–1978), he held a post there (~1980–2015) and has served as a lecturer at ICPBS and IIBS (attested 2026).

Masataro Sawayanagi (1865–1927) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1885–1888). He later held posts at Tokyo University of Education (~1901–1910), Tohoku University (~1911–1913), Kyushu University (~1913–1914), and Taisho University (~1926–1927).

Masato Fujii (b. 1956) is an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at Osaka University and under Asko Parpola at the University of Helsinki (doctorate 2004), he served as a professor at Kyoto University from 1993 to 2020.

Masato Kobayashi (b. 1970) specializes in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and under George Cardona at the University of Pennsylvania (Ph.D. ~2000), subsequently working at TUFS and becoming a professor at the University of Tokyo (~2018).

Masatoshi Konishi (1938–2020) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at ICU, Calcutta, Tokyo, and Rikkyo universities, and served on the faculties of Hosei University (1971–1984) and Rikkyo University (1984–2003).

Masatoshi Nagatomi (1926–2000) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Ryukoku, Kyoto, and Harvard University (Ph.D. under Daniel H. H. Ingalls), he was appointed Instructor of Sanskrit at Harvard in 1958 and trained numerous prominent scholars.

Masayuki Taira (b. 1951) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1971–1980) and held posts at Kansai University (~1983–1992), Osaka University (~1992–2016), and Kyoto Tachibana University (~2016–2021).
